# hermes-lcm-ledger v1.0.0

LCM Ledger 1.0.0 is the first stable release of the Hermes-LCM fork maintained by Benjamin Wittorf. It promotes the RC2 runtime and archive format. Hermes-LCM was created by Stephen Schoettler and contributors. [Upstream project](https://github.com/stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm) · [Original fork changes in PR #589](https://github.com/stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm/pull/589)

## Install or upgrade

LCM Ledger supports Hermes Agent 0.23.4 through the 0.x series with Python 3.14. On a fresh profile, install the plugin and select its context engine.

```sh
hermes plugins install ben-wf/hermes-lcm-ledger --enable
hermes config set context.engine lcm
```

Existing Ledger installations keep their `lcm.db`, profile settings and engine key. Standard GitHub installs track the default branch. For an installation pinned to this release, use the full commit SHA for this tag with the Hermes installer’s `--ref` option. To switch from the original Hermes-LCM plugin, follow the [migration guide](https://github.com/ben-wf/hermes-lcm-ledger/blob/v1.0.0/README.md#switching-from-hermes-lcm).

## What ships in 1.0

- A leaf summary and its restart checkpoint commit together. Long conversations retain access to higher-level summaries beyond the first 1,000 nodes.
- Ingestion and full-text recall continue during SQLite online backups. Concurrent rotations coordinate their snapshots and preserve a usable restore point.
- Recall returns source excerpts with verifiable character offsets. Compatible Hermes hosts keep the static recall guidance in the session prompt.
- Desktop shows the resolved profile settings and, when available, the settings loaded by the focused chat.

## Tested operating range

On Apple Silicon, a synthetic archive containing 1,191,680 messages occupied 7.50 GB. During three online backups with the default eight-second recall budget, all 489 searches returned their expected excerpts and all 4,942 excerpts matched the original text at the reported offset. The backups took 14.8–18.0 seconds while ingestion continued.

Search breadth matters. During backup, the 95th-percentile response time was 27 ms for targeted lookups and 996 ms for a term matching 1,358 messages. In a separate stress run with a 150 ms budget, 46 of 47 broad searches timed out. Across both budgets all six backups reopened successfully and passed SQLite integrity, message checksum, index and source-excerpt checks.
